questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: pH from reactions with Na2CO3 and NH4Cl
concepts: pH from reactions with Na2CO3 and NH4Cl
questions.question:
Unknown solutions are labelled as P, Q and R. The table shows some of the reactions of the solutions with sodium carbonate and solid ammonium chloride:
P: with sodium carbonate - gas evolved; with solid ammonium chloride - no reaction
Q: with sodium carbonate - no reaction; with solid ammonium chloride - gas evolved
R: with sodium carbonate - no reaction; with solid ammonium chloride - no reaction
The correct pH of the three solutions are:
questions.solution: (c) P = 2, Q = 13, R = 7. P liberates CO2 from carbonate, so it is an acid (pH 2); Q liberates NH3 from an ammonium salt, so it is an alkali (pH 13); R is neutral (pH 7).

questions.question: Salt A gave reddish brown precipitate with ammonium hydroxide and white precipitate with barium chloride which is insoluble in dil HCl. Salt A is:
questions.solution: (a) Ferric sulphate. Reddish-brown Fe(OH)3 shows Fe3+; white BaSO4 insoluble in dil. HCl shows sulphate.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Four set-ups are shown: 1. calcium carbonate heated in a dish over a burner; 2. zinc in dilute hydrochloric acid in a flask; 3. ethanol in a spirit lamp (labelled 'Conc sulphuric acid'); 4. magnesium carbonate in dilute sulphuric acid in a flask.
Which reaction produces water?
questions.solution: (d) 3 and 4. Ethanol gives water on burning (or on dehydration with conc. H2SO4: C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O); MgCO3 + H2SO4 -> MgSO4 + H2O + CO2. 1 gives CaO + CO2 and 2 gives ZnCl2 + H2.

questions.question: A is an ionic compound. B is a covalent compound having three bond pairs and one lone pair. C is a non-polar covalent compound. A, B and C are:

options.a: A: sodium chloride, B: nitrogen molecule, C: ammonia
options.b: A: nitrogen molecule, B: sodium chloride, C: ammonia
options.c: A: sodium chloride, B: ammonia, C: nitrogen molecule
options.d: A: ammonia, B: sodium chloride, C: nitrogen molecule

questions.solution: (c) A: sodium chloride, B: ammonia, C: nitrogen molecule. NaCl is ionic; NH3 has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on N; N2 is a non-polar covalent molecule.

questions.question: Ammonia reacts with compound A to give pinkish brown metal. Compound A is ______. Property exhibited by ammonia is ______.
questions.solution: (a) CuO, reducing agent. 3CuO + 2NH3 -> 3Cu (pinkish-brown) + 3H2O + N2; ammonia acts as a reducing agent.

questions.question: Which of the following is false for ionic compounds?

options.a: Ionic compounds are soluble in water
options.b: Ionic compounds have low melting point and low boiling point
options.c: Ionic compounds in aqueous state are good conductors of electricity
options.d: Ionic compounds are held together by electrostatic force of attraction

questions.solution: (b) Ionic compounds have low melting point and low boiling point. Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points due to strong electrostatic forces.

questions.question:
Sample P: 0.25 moles of sulphuric acid [at. wt. H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
Sample Q: 11.2 L of CO2 [at. wt. C = 12, O = 16]
Sample R: 6.023 x 10^22 molecules of glucose [mol. wt. of glucose = 180]
Sample S: 21 g of NaOH
The correct order of increasing weight shall be:
questions.solution: (a) P > Q > S > R. P = 0.25 x 98 = 24.5 g; Q = 0.5 mol x 44 = 22 g; R = 0.1 mol x 180 = 18 g; S = 21 g. So P > Q > S > R (i.e. increasing order R < S < Q < P). (Printed option labels are a, b, c, e; the fourth is treated as d.)

questions.question: Compound A reacts with NaOH to give a gas B. B gives dense white fumes with glass rod dipped in HCl. A is:
questions.solution: (d) Ammonium chloride. NH4Cl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O + NH3; NH3 gives dense white fumes of NH4Cl with HCl.

questions.question: Ethyl bromide reacts with alcoholic KOH to give ______ and the reaction is known as ______.
questions.solution: (d) Ethene, dehydrohalogenation. C2H5Br + KOH (alc.) -> C2H4 + KBr + H2O, elimination of HBr (dehydrohalogenation).

questions.question: The correct order of electron affinity in halogens is:
questions.solution: (d) Cl > F > Br. Chlorine has the highest electron affinity; fluorine's very small size causes inter-electronic repulsion, so its EA is lower than Cl but higher than Br.

questions.question: Product formed at anode and cathode when molten lead bromide is electrolysed using iron electrode at cathode and anode are ______ and ______ respectively.
questions.solution: (d) Br2, Pb. Br- is oxidised to Br2 at the anode; Pb2+ is reduced to Pb at the cathode.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Ammonia is collected by downward displacement of air.
Reason (R): Ammonia is lighter than air.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Ammonia (VD 8.5) is lighter than air (VD 14.4), so it is collected by downward displacement of air; R explains A.

questions.question:
Structures shown: A = ethane (H3C-CH3), B = ethene (H2C=CH2), C = ethanol (CH3-CH2-OH).
P: A is formed when sodium propanoate is treated with sodalime.
Q: B is formed when C is treated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 170 C.
R: B on reacting with H2 and Ni at high temperature gives A.

options.a: P, Q and R are correct
options.b: Only P and Q are correct
options.c: Only Q and R are correct
options.d: Only P and R are correct

questions.solution: (a) P, Q and R are correct. C2H5COONa + NaOH -> C2H6 + Na2CO3; C2H5OH -(conc. H2SO4, 170 C)-> C2H4 + H2O; C2H4 + H2 -(Ni)-> C2H6. All three are correct.

questions.question: What volume of hydrogen gas shall be liberated when 130 g of zinc reacts completely with HCl? [At. wt. of Zn = 65]
questions.solution: (b) 44.8 L. Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2; 130/65 = 2 mol Zn gives 2 mol H2 = 2 x 22.4 = 44.8 L at STP.

questions.question: A compound Z on heating gives black colour residue and liberates a reddish-brown gas. Compound Z is:
questions.solution: (b) Copper nitrate. 2Cu(NO3)2 -> 2CuO (black) + 4NO2 (reddish brown) + O2.

questions.question:
Solve the following:
(a) 2C4H10 + 13O2 -> 8CO2 + 10H2O. Calculate the following when 60 L of butane is completely combusted:
(i) Volume of oxygen required for complete combustion of 60 L of butane
(ii) Volume of carbon dioxide liberated during the same process
(b) A flask contains 3.4 g of ammonia. Calculate:
(i) the moles of ammonia
(ii) the number of molecules of ammonia in the flask
(iii) the volume occupied by 3.4 g of ammonia at s.t.p. (at. wt. N = 14, H = 1)
questions.solution:
(a)(i) 2 vol butane : 13 vol O2 -> O2 = 60 x 13/2 = 390 L
(ii) 2 vol butane : 8 vol CO2 -> CO2 = 60 x 8/2 = 240 L
(b)(i) Molar mass NH3 = 17 g; moles = 3.4/17 = 0.2 mol
(ii) molecules = 0.2 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 1.2044 x 10^23
(iii) volume = 0.2 x 22.4 = 4.48 L

questions.question:
Match the following:
Column A: (a) Solder (b) Brass (c) C7H14 (d) C8H18 (e) C9H16
Column B: i. Alkane ii. Alkene iii. Alkyne iv. Copper and zinc v. Lead and tin
questions.solution: (a)-v (solder: lead and tin); (b)-iv (brass: copper and zinc); (c)-ii (C7H14 fits CnH2n, alkene); (d)-i (C8H18 fits CnH2n+2, alkane); (e)-iii (C9H16 fits CnH2n-2, alkyne).

questions.question:
Complete the following by choosing the correct options from the brackets:
(a) ______ (AgNO3 / BaCl2 / lead nitrate) cannot be used to distinguish between copper nitrate and zinc chloride.
(b) A special type of covalent bond where both the electrons are given by same atom for sharing is known as ______ (metallic / coordinate / hydrogen) bond.
(c) Element A is from group 2, element B is from group 16. Formula when A combines with B is ______ (AB, AB2, A2B).
(d) Process by which superior metal is plated over inferior metal by electrolysis is known as ______ (electrometallurgy / electrorefining / electroplating).
(e) ______ (conc sulphuric acid / CaO / NH3) is used as drying agent for lab preparation of HCl.

answer_items.prompt: (a) cannot distinguish copper nitrate and zinc chloride
(b) bond with both electrons from one atom
(d) plating a superior metal over an inferior one

(a) BaCl2 - neither salt contains sulphate, so neither gives a precipitate (AgNO3 and lead nitrate give a white chloride precipitate with ZnCl2 only).
(b) coordinate
(c) AB (valency 2 and 2)
(d) electroplating
(e) conc. sulphuric acid

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Electrolysis of copper sulphate solution is widely used for the purification of copper in industries. When an aqueous solution of copper sulphate (CuSO4) is taken in a voltameter and copper plates are used as both electrodes, an interesting change takes place. The solution contains positively charged copper ions (Cu2+) and negatively charged sulphate ions (SO4 2-). This method is highly important as it helps produce copper of very high purity for electrical wires and electronic components. (Diagram: copper anode connected to + terminal and copper cathode to - terminal of a battery, dipping in aqueous copper sulphate.)
(i) State the reaction at cathode.
(ii) State the reaction at anode.
(iii) Explain: blue colour of copper sulphate remains as blue in above experiment.
(iv) What shall be the observation when platinum is taken as anode electrode instead of copper electrode?
(v) Define: electrorefining.
questions.solution:
(i) Cathode: Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu
(ii) Anode: Cu - 2e- -> Cu2+ (Cu -> Cu2+ + 2e-)
(iii) For every Cu2+ ion discharged at the cathode, one Cu2+ ion enters the solution from the copper anode, so the Cu2+ concentration (and the blue colour) stays the same.
(iv) With an inert Pt anode, OH- ions are discharged and bubbles of oxygen gas are seen at the anode; the blue colour of the solution gradually fades as Cu2+ ions are deposited (solution becomes acidic).
(v) Electrorefining: the process of purifying an impure metal by electrolysis, in which the impure metal is the anode, a thin strip of pure metal is the cathode and a salt solution of the metal is the electrolyte.

marking_points.point: O2 at anode and blue colour fades

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Give reason:
(a) Conc. sulphuric acid cannot be used as drying agent for ammonia.
(b) In Haber's process, unreacted H2 and N2 gas are separated from ammonia by liquefaction or by dissolving in water.
questions.solution:
(a) Ammonia is basic and reacts with conc. sulphuric acid: 2NH3 + H2SO4 -> (NH4)2SO4, so the ammonia would be absorbed.
(b) Ammonia is easily liquefied (and highly soluble in water) whereas N2 and H2 are not, so NH3 can be separated and the unreacted gases recycled.

marking_points.point: NH3 is basic and reacts with H2SO4
NH3 easily liquefied / highly soluble unlike N2 and H2

(b) Cl, F, Br, I [increasing electronegativity]

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Answer the following:
(a) Al2O3.2H2O --NaOH--> A + H2O; A --H2O, heat--> B + NaOH; B --1100 C--> C + H2O. Identify A, B and C.
(b) Name of the process which converts bauxite to pure alumina.
(c) Product formed at cathode and anode during electrolysis by Hall-Heroult's process.
(d) Why cannot pure alumina be converted to aluminium using reducing agent?
questions.solution:
(a) A = sodium aluminate (NaAlO2): Al2O3.2H2O + 2NaOH -> 2NaAlO2 + 3H2O
B = aluminium hydroxide, Al(OH)3: NaAlO2 + 2H2O -> NaOH + Al(OH)3
C = alumina, Al2O3: 2Al(OH)3 -(1100 C)-> Al2O3 + 3H2O
(b) Baeyer's process
(c) Cathode: aluminium (Al3+ + 3e- -> Al); anode: oxygen (which burns the carbon anode to CO2)
(d) Aluminium is highly electropositive (high in the activity series) and has a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon, so common reducing agents cannot reduce alumina; it is reduced electrolytically.

marking_points.point: Al at cathode, O2 at anode
Al is highly reactive / greater affinity for oxygen

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
From the equation: (NH4)2Cr2O7 -> N2(g) + 4H2O(g) + Cr2O3, calculate the following:
(i) the quantity in moles of (NH4)2Cr2O7 if 63 g of (NH4)2Cr2O7 is heated
(ii) the quantity in moles of N2 formed
(iii) the volume in litres or dm3 of N2 evolved at s.t.p. [at. wt. N = 14, Cr = 52, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.solution:
Molar mass of (NH4)2Cr2O7 = 2(14 + 4) + 2(52) + 7(16) = 36 + 104 + 112 = 252 g
(i) moles = 63/252 = 0.25 mol
(ii) 1 mol gives 1 mol N2, so N2 = 0.25 mol
(iii) volume = 0.25 x 22.4 = 5.6 dm3

questions.question: A compound contains carbon 14.4%, hydrogen 1.2% and chlorine 84.5%. Determine the empirical formula of this compound. The relative molecular mass of compound is 168, so what is its molecular formula? [C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5]

questions.question:
For the lab preparation of HCl (apparatus: round-bottom flask containing sodium chloride heated on a tripod, with a dropping funnel containing liquid A; the gas passes through a wash bottle B containing a liquid and is collected in an upright gas jar labelled 'Hydrogen chloride'):
(a) Identify A and B.
(b) Write balanced equation of A with NaCl below 200 C.
(c) Why is HCl gas not collected over water?
questions.solution:
(a) A = concentrated sulphuric acid (reactant in the dropping funnel); B = wash bottle with concentrated sulphuric acid, used as the drying agent.
(b) NaCl + H2SO4 (conc.) -(below 200 C)-> NaHSO4 + HCl
(c) HCl is highly soluble in water, so it would dissolve instead of being collected.

questions.question:
Distinguish between the following pairs of salts:
(a) Sodium nitrate and sodium sulphide [using dil HCl]
(b) Copper sulphate solution and calcium nitrate solution [using excess ammonium hydroxide solution]
(c) Dil HCl solution and dil H2SO4 solution [using BaCl2 solution]

questions.question:
Draw electron dot structure for the following:
(a) water [at. number O = 8, H = 1]
(b) calcium chloride [at. number Ca = 20, Cl = 17]
(c) ammonium ion [atomic number H = 1, N = 7]
questions.solution:
(a) H2O: O shares one electron pair with each H (two single covalent bonds); O keeps two lone pairs, giving an octet.
(b) CaCl2: Ca (2,8,8,2) transfers one electron to each of two Cl atoms (2,8,7): [Ca]2+ and 2[:Cl:]- with full octets, shown in brackets with charges.

questions.question:
Some elements are given in their own symbol and position in the periodic table, while others are shown with a letter with reference to the table. Identify:
Period 2: Group 1 - A; Group 2 - Be; Group 16 - O; Group 17 - Z; Group 18 - Ne
Period 3: Group 1 - Na; Group 2 - Mg; Group 13 - D; Group 14 - P; Group 16 - Y; Group 17 - G; Group 18 - Ar
Period 4: Group 1 - B; Group 2 - Ca; Group 15 - E; Group 16 - X; Group 18 - Kr
(a) Element with largest atomic size in period 4 (except the noble gas) and mention the type of bond made by that element with Z.
(b) Element with most electron affinity in group 17 and mention its formulae with element P.
(c) Number of valence electrons of X and mention its formulae with D element.
questions.solution:
(a) B (potassium, group 1); B with Z (fluorine) forms an ionic (electrovalent) bond - BZ.
(b) G (chlorine) has the highest electron affinity in group 17; with P (silicon, valency 4) the formula is PG4.
(c) X (group 16) has 6 valence electrons (valency 2); with D (aluminium, valency 3) the formula is D2X3.
